{"id": "0efa23d7-9e61-40fd-bfd0-5d54e74fc557", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "ALB vs NLB Load Balancer Differences Explained"}]}

{"id": "8b273a16-b488-4edd-857a-fbe05b6d4eab", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Application Load Balancers (ALB) and Network Load Balancers (NLB) work at different layers of the network stack, so they suit different workloads.

| | **ALB** | **NLB** |
|---|---|---|
| **OSI layer** | Layer 7 (application) | Layer 4 (transport) |
| **Protocols** | HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, WebSocket | TCP, UDP, TLS, TCP_UDP |
| **Routing** | Content-based. Rules match on path, host header, HTTP method, headers, query strings, or source IP. | Connection-based. Routes on IP, port, and protocol. |
| **Performance** | Good for web traffic. It inspects each request, so latency is higher. | Very high throughput and ultra-low latency. It handles millions of requests per second and sudden traffic spikes. |
| **IP addressing** | The DNS name resolves to IPs that can change. Static IPs aren't supported. | One static IP per Availability Zone, and you can attach Elastic IPs. This makes it easy to allowlist. |
| **Client IP preservation** | The client IP is passed in the `X-Forwarded-For` header. | The client source IP is preserved by default for instance targets. |
| **Targets** | Instances, IPs, Lambda functions, containers | Instances, IPs, and ALBs (you can put an NLB in front of an ALB) |
| **Security groups** | Supported | Supported (added in 2023), but optional |
| **Built-in features** | Redirects, fixed responses, authentication (Cognito/OIDC), WAF integration, sticky sessions, weighted target groups | TLS termination, PrivateLink support (endpoint services), preserved source IP |
| **TLS** | Terminates HTTPS and supports SNI | Can terminate TLS or pass it through untouched |

**Choose an ALB when:**
- You run HTTP/HTTPS apps such as web apps, REST APIs, or microservices.
- You need path-based or host-based routing, for example `/api` to one service and `/images` to another.
- You want WAF, user authentication, or Lambda targets.

**Choose an NLB when:**
- You need extreme performance or very low latency.
- You have non-HTTP protocols such as gaming, IoT, VoIP, or custom TCP/UDP services.
- You need static or Elastic IPs, for example for customers who allowlist your IPs.
- You want to expose a service through AWS PrivateLink.

A common pattern is to put an NLB in front of an ALB. That gives you static IPs and PrivateLink while keeping Layer 7 routing.

I can also look at the load balancers in your own AWS account to see which type each one is and how it's configured.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
